propositions: A write whose lock acquire() times out within the budget is permanently discarded with no retry or queue, causing data loss

Current single-deadline architecture treats the `attempts` parameter as a silent multiplier rather than a retry loop, and both fcntl and mkdir legs poll non-blocking with jitter, creating lottery-style unfair arbitration

Holder duration (not writer count) now drives loss on production: a 70s holder + 3 comments loses all 3 writes with 0 markers persisted afterward; claim succeeds only on attempts=1 budget and fails at exactly 30.30s
Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts loss to latency without phantom-write risk, because retries exhaust only the acquisition step before the caller's write body runs

Five call sites opt into retries via REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped [0,10]) with per-pass warnings and cumulative-wait messages in LockTimeout; all other callers retain fail-fast via retries=0 default

Plan-review gate's own PASS verdict was destroyed twice by this bug (holders at 103s and 88s exceed 60s budget but sit inside planned ~181.5s retry ceiling), demonstrating bootstrap deadlock where the gate cannot certify its own fix
